text:
Alex: Heads up — we need to agree on the rollout plan for Tenant Prime (Q2 initiative). I want a short decision thread for flags, canary cohorts, and fallback ordering.
Nina: +1. Can we keep the initial scope minimal? core routing + simple billing tag, no fancy UI A/B yet.
Sam: Agree on minimal. Also need to confirm SRE's latency SLO acceptance if we enable model-v2 for 5% traffic.
Jen: SLOs: target p95 <= 220ms, error rate < 0.5% for the canary slice. If either threshold is breached for 10m continuous, auto-fallback.
Alex: Good. Proposed slices: 0.5% internal-only -> 2% alpha cohort (partners) -> 5% public canary -> 25% ramp. Thoughts?
Nina: Looks fine. Add a rollback kill-switch accessible to product and SRE. Name it flag: tenant_prime.enabled and flag: tenant_prime.killswitch.
Sam: For orchestration, prefer split by geozone + tenant tier. e.g., europe/na for alpha, rest for later. Also we should shadow traffic to model-v2 for 100% before ramp (no responses returned).
Jen: Shadowing OK. Make sure KV cache warmup is part of alpha checklist — cold starts killed our p50 in last test.
Alex: I'll draft the rollout playbook. Quick sketch:
```
- flags:
  - tenant_prime.enabled (bool)
  - tenant_prime.variant = [v1, v2, v2-quant]
  - tenant_prime.slice = [internal, partners, public]
- cohorts:
  - internal: 0.5% (dev orgs)
  - partners: 2% (signed partners)
  - public-canary: 5% (geo-sampled)
- fallback order:
  1) v2 -> v2-quant (if perf ok)
  2) v2 -> v1 (if quality/regressions)
  3) traffic -> dedicated cold fallback pool
- stop criteria:
  - p95 > 220ms for 10m
  - error_rate > 0.5% for 10m
  - quality delta (eval set) > 2% drop
```
Sam: Couple of asks: add a rate-limiter ramp to protect downstream DBs, and ensure token-level cost accounting per route so finance can see delta.
Nina: Also need to lock the experiment window: 72h min, but allow manual extend with product lead + SRE signoff.
Jen: For automatic fallback, implement a two-step: first throttle to 50% for 5m, if metrics still bad then full rollback. That avoids abrupt UX disruption.
Alex: Good call. We should also define observability signals: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-ver mismatch, freshness of KV cache, useful prompt-level error counter.
ops-bot: Deploy check: infra-canary passed (green) — image: tenant-prime:v2-rc4 deployed to eu-canary at 2026-03-23T10:21Z
Sam: ops-bot — please also capture cold-start traces and snapshot KV hit-rate every 15s during alpha.
ops-bot: Noted. Will post traces under /observability/tenant-prime/alpha.
Nina: We should pre-seed cache for top 10 tenants in partners slice. I'll coordinate with solutions-eng to get sample prompts.
Alex: Who owns the feature flag gating cadence? I can own product signoffs; need SRE to confirm auto-fallback implementation and infra to own rollout script.
Jen: SRE owns auto-fallback. infra owns rollout automation and feature-flag API changes. Product owns cohort selection and customer comms.
Sam: Let's add an A/B evaluation plan for the partners slice: 50/50 v1 vs v2 with these KPIs: latency, failure rate, completion quality (ratios from eval harness).
Alex: Action items:
- Alex: write playbook and cherry-pick kill-switch perms (today)
- Jen: implement throttle-first fallback + metrics (by EOD tomorrow)
- Sam: setup shadowing + cold-start traces (by EOD tomorrow)
- Nina: prepare partner prompts and cache pre-seed list (by Tue)
- infra: prepare rollout automation & flag naming (blocker: update ff service to support variant tagging)
Jen: I'll schedule a 30m shiproom for cutover runbook after playbook draft.
Alex: OK — if nobody objects, we'll start internal slice tomorrow morning 09:00 UTC. Final call?
Nina: No objections. :thumbsup:
Sam: No objections from SRE.
Jen: +1 from infra/SRE on schedule.
Alex: Great — I'll post the playbook link once done and tag everyone for the shiproom.
Nina: thanks all.
